official.deadline_note: Applications for the currently open Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 scholarships close November 1, 2026; the Fall 2027 and 2027-2028 academic year applications run February 1, 2027 - March 1, 2027. The official page states application deadlines are subject to change.
official.application_cycle: Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 cycle (October 1 - November 1, 2026); Fall 2027 and 2027-2028 academic year cycle (February 1 - March 1, 2027)
official.status_note: The official page states: 'Applications for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 scholarships will be accepted October 1, 2026 - November 1, 2026.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording: TAMS 'provides a waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition bill' and 'is not a cash award'; the Good Neighbor Scholarship 'provides an exemption of one year's worth of tuition (fall, spring, and summer)' but 'does not pay for any fees or charges on the tuition bill, such as health insurance, late registration fees, ISSS Support Services fee'; the African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship includes 'a tuition waiver (of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition bill) for the academic year'; the General ISSS Financial Aid award 'does not provide a waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition & fee bill'.
official.funding_period: one-time award per semester or academic year
benefits: Spring-term tuition scholarships: $5,000 Carlos and Clara Quintanilla Scholarship, $4,500 Ethel Loving de Diaz Scholarship, $3,500 Society of Iranian-American Women for Education (SIAWE) Scholarship, and $2,000 Dr. David Nilsson Scholarship

Fall and academic-year tuition scholarships: $4,800 STEM Scholarship (fall), $5,000 Iimura Peace Endowed Scholarship (fall), $3,500 Jerry D. Wilcox Community Engagement Scholarship (fall), and $2,500 Khalid Alhilali Memorial Scholarship (fall)

African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship: a $5,000 academic year scholarship with a tuition waiver (of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition bill), divided in half with $2,500 disbursed in the fall and $2,500 in the spring

Tuition Assistance for Mexican Students (TAMS): a waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition bill; the award is not a cash award and is administered through Texas Global on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board

Good Neighbor Scholarship (GNS): an exemption of one year's worth of tuition (fall, spring, and summer) for eligible students born in and resident of a nation in the Western Hemisphere; administered through Texas Global on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board

General ISSS Financial Aid and the International Education Fee Scholarship (IEFS): cash scholarships for students who demonstrate financial need; IEFS was initially established in 1989 by a student referendum
eligibility: You are an undergraduate or graduate student enrolled full-time at UT Austin during the award semester
Most awards require you to have completed an entire course of study for two academic semesters at UT Austin (two semesters by the time the award is disbursed for Jerry D. Wilcox)

Minimum cumulative GPA set per award, ranging from 2.0 to 3.75 (2.0 undergraduate / 3.0 graduate satisfactory progress for Ethel Loving de Diaz; 3.0 undergraduate / 3.75 graduate for SIAWE; 3.0 for African Leadership Bridge; 3.25 for Jerry D. Wilcox; 2.0 for Quintanilla, Nilsson, Iimura Peace and Khalid Alhilali)
You can demonstrate financial need (General ISSS Financial Aid, Quintanilla, Nilsson, Ethel Loving de Diaz, SIAWE, African Leadership Bridge, Khalid Alhilali)

Country or region of origin conditions: resided in Mexico immediately prior to enrolling (Quintanilla); graduated from a high school in Mexico (Nilsson); lived in or matriculated from a school in Iran (SIAWE); preparatory education on the African continent (African Leadership Bridge); matriculated from a high school in East Asia or Asia (Iimura Peace); part or all preparatory schooling in the Middle East (Khalid Alhilali); born in and a resident of a Western Hemisphere nation (Good Neighbor)
General ISSS Financial Aid is only available for formula-funded courses (Option I); Option III students are not eligible
requirements: Scholarship applications are accepted via LASSO, the university-wide scholarship system; find them with the keyword search 'ISSS'
Applicants should be prepared to answer questions about their estimated annual expenses
Applicants should be prepared to write essays related to the scholarship's intent or their own experiences and background
Applicants must meet all eligibility criteria to apply
Iimura Peace Endowed Scholarship recipients are required to complete a Service Project within one year of receiving the scholarship
Maintain full-time enrollment at UT Austin during the semester in which the scholarship is awarded
documents: Completed LASSO scholarship application located by the keyword 'ISSS'
Responses within the application on your estimated annual expenses
Essays related to the scholarship's intent or your own experiences and background
selection_criteria: Demonstrated financial need for the need-based awards
Academic standing and the minimum cumulative GPA published for each specific award

Published award preferences: first-generation status and work experience funding education (Ethel Loving de Diaz); high school in Tejupilco or the state of Queretaro (Dr. David Nilsson); matriculation from a high school or university in Monterrey, Mexico, then other Mexican cities (STEM); incoming first-year students (African Leadership Bridge)
Leadership and positive contributions through participation in campus/community organizations (Jerry D. Wilcox)
Awards are competitive and the number allotted per semester is limited (General ISSS Financial Aid; TAMS is not guaranteed due to limited awards)
coverage: One-time cash awards designated as tuition scholarships for the semester or academic year granted: published amounts of $2,000, $2,500, $3,500, $4,500, $4,800 and $5,000 depending on the award
TAMS: waiver of the nonresident portion of a student's tuition bill - not a cash award
African Leadership Bridge Endowed Scholarship: $5,000 academic year award plus a tuition waiver of the nonresident portion of the student's tuition bill

Good Neighbor Scholarship: exemption of one year's worth of tuition (fall, spring, and summer); the exemption does not pay for any fees or charges on the tuition bill, such as health insurance, late registration fees, or the ISSS Support Services fee
All cash awards will automatically apply to any outstanding UT debts upon disbursement; award amounts in excess of debts will be distributed to the student's direct deposit account
14% of the scholarship will be withheld for tax purposes per US tax law, unless a tax treaty for scholarships is in effect or the recipient is considered a resident alien for tax purposes
application_method: During an open window, log in to LASSO (utexas.scholarships.ngwebsolutions.com) with your UT Austin account
On the Scholarship Search page use the keyword search 'ISSS' and click the 'Apply Now' button at the top right
After logging in, review all currently open applications you may be eligible to complete in the Task section
Find your desired scholarship application and click 'Start Application' or 'Continue Application'
Answer the estimated annual expenses questions and complete the essays, then submit before the window deadline
Questions can be emailed to intlfinaid@austin.utexas.edu (responses within 2-3 business days)
official.application_route: Apply online through LASSO, the university-wide scholarship system, by searching the keyword 'ISSS' during one of the twice-yearly application windows (October 1 - November 1 for spring/summer awards; February 1 - March 1 for fall/academic-year awards).
official.study_mode: Full-time enrollment at UT Austin during the award semester
official.citizenship_residency: Awards are open to international students enrolled at UT Austin; several are restricted by country or region of origin (Mexico, Iran, Africa, Middle East, East Asia/Asia) and the Good Neighbor Scholarship requires students to have been born in and be residents of a nation in the Western Hemisphere
official.international_eligibility: Yes - these scholarships are administered by ISSS specifically for international students at UT Austin
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Field restrictions on some awards: Cockrell School of Engineering enrollment (Quintanilla and the STEM Scholarship's engineering programs); any Dell Medical School degree or College of Natural Sciences programs excluding Human Development and Family Sciences, Textiles and Apparel, Public Health, and Ecology, Evolution and Behavior (STEM); undergraduate-only awards (Nilsson, African Leadership Bridge, Iimura Peace, Jerry D. Wilcox, Khalid Alhilali). TAMS and the Good Neighbor Scholarship are administered through Texas Global on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board.
official.duration: One-time awards for the semester or academic year in which they are granted; recipients are not guaranteed to receive the scholarship in subsequent years
official.description: Texas Global's International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS) administers a portfolio of one-time scholarships for international students enrolled at UT Austin, awarded twice a year through LASSO. The portfolio combines need-based, merit-based and country-restricted cash tuition awards - published at amounts from $2,000 to $5,000 - with nonresident tuition waivers and the Good Neighbor one-year tuition exemption administered on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board.
official.region: North America (The University of Texas at Austin, United States)
official.program_type: University-administered needs-based, merit-based and country-restricted scholarships, one-time cash tuition awards and tuition waivers/exemptions for enrolled international students

not_confirmed: funding_amount - the official page publishes no single programme-wide amount; per-award published amounts of $2,000-$5,000 and tuition waivers are documented in benefits and coverage
english_requirement - not published on the official scholarships page
research_requirement - no research-proposal requirement is published
verification.notes: All amounts, deadlines, eligibility rules, coverage wording and application steps were taken from the official Texas Global/ISSS Scholarships and Financial Services page (deadline, cycle and status cross-checked against its Spring 2027/Summer 2027 window of October 1 - November 1, 2026); tax-withholding wording cross-checked against the official ISSS Filing a Tax Return page. Because this is a multi-award programme with no single published figure, funding_amount is null and individual award amounts are quoted verbatim.

applicant_utility.summary: Every award here requires full-time enrollment at UT Austin first, and most also demand two completed UT semesters, so treat this as mid-degree funding rather than an entry ticket. The two entry windows are short and fixed - October 1 to November 1 for spring/summer awards and February 1 to March 1 for fall/academic-year awards - so plan your LASSO essays before each window opens. Budget around two mechanics that reduce what you actually keep: cash awards are applied to any outstanding UT debt before reaching your account, and 14% is withheld for tax unless a treaty applies or you are a resident alien for tax purposes.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Continuing international undergraduates and graduates at UT Austin with at least two completed semesters, demonstrated financial need, and - for the country-restricted awards - prep-school or residency ties to Mexico, Iran, Africa, the Middle East, East Asia or a Western Hemisphere nation.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will have completed an entire course of study for two academic semesters at UT Austin by the disbursement date if your target award requires it
Check your graduate funding option before relying on General ISSS Financial Aid - Option III students are not eligible
Verify your cumulative GPA against the specific award's floor (2.0 to 3.75 depending on award and level) and plan to maintain it for the award duration
Draft a separate essay for each award rather than reusing one text, since prompts follow each scholarship's stated intent
Prepare your estimated annual expenses figure in advance - the application asks for it
Diary the window openings (October 1 and February 1) and re-check LASSO, since the official page warns deadlines are subject to change
common_rejection_risks: Missing the only two annual entry windows - October 1 - November 1 or February 1 - March 1
Having fewer than two completed UT semesters by the time the award disburses for the awards that require it
Falling below the award-specific GPA minimum or failing to maintain the minimum for the award duration
Applying for General ISSS Financial Aid as an Option III student
Generic essays that ignore the award's stated intent or preference criteria (first-generation, Tejupilco/Queretaro, Monterrey, incoming first-year)
Applying inside the wrong term's window or missing that awards are one-time with no renewal guarantee
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Nonresident tuition beyond the TAMS, Good Neighbor and African Leadership Bridge waivers; fees explicitly excluded from the Good Neighbor exemption (health insurance, late registration fees, ISSS Support Services fee); all living expenses in Austin; and travel. Short-term institutional loans exist (tuition loan up to $5,000 and emergency cash loan up to $500 at 4.00% APR) but must be repaid, with a financial hold and 25% collection fee if loans go four months past due.
document_audit: No transcripts or test scores are uploaded - eligibility is verified through your UT records, so an enrollment or GPA issue kills the application before essays are read
Essays are the real differentiator: answer each award's intent and its published preference criteria explicitly
Make the estimated-annual-expenses answers consistent with your actual UT budget, since they feed the need assessment
Expect scholarship income to be taxable paperwork: a 1042-S is issued for scholarship income and nonresidents must file even when tax was withheld
alerts: Cash awards are applied to outstanding UT debts first, so any balance due directly shrinks what you receive
14% tax withholding applies unless a scholarship tax treaty covers you or you are a resident alien for tax purposes
All awards are one-time - winning this year does not carry into the next
Iimura Peace winners must complete a service project within one year of receiving the award
The number of awards per semester is limited and the process is competitive, especially for General ISSS Financial Aid and TAMS
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Applications are submitted entirely inside LASSO during an open window: search the keyword 'ISSS', open the application from your Tasks list, complete the expense questions and essays, and submit before the deadline.
